elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Doubling Consonants (1-1-1 Rule) & Short Vowel Signalling
1. Definition: In a 1-syllable word with 1 vowel and 1 ending consonant, double the consonant before adding a vowel suffix.

2. Rule: 1-1-1 Rule: 1 syllable + 1 vowel + 1 consonant + vowel suffix (-ed, -ing, -er) = double consonant (stop -> stopped). Multi-syllable: double only if final syllable is stressed (adMIT -> admitting vs VISit -> visiting).
3. Why? The double consonant acts as a wall protecting the short vowel from becoming long.
4. How to recognize? Compare dinner (double n = short i) vs diner (single n = long i).
5. Common examples: stop -> stopped/stopping, run -> running, plan -> planned, dinner /ˈdɪnər/ vs diner /ˈdaɪnər/
6. Counter-examples: Words with 2 vowels (treat -> treated) or 2 consonants (help -> helped).
7. Exceptions: British English doubles final L regardless of stress (travel -> travelled).
8. Common mistakes: Forgetting to double in 'hoping' vs 'hopping' causing meaning shifts.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Double consonant = Short vowel! Single consonant = Long vowel!
10. Key vocabulary: 1-1-1 rule, doubling, short vowel signal, vowel suffix, stress-conditioned
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟡 A2
13. Associated Visual: 🛡️ Double consonant wall protecting short vowel.
14. Key Takeaway: 1-1-1 = Double the consonant! Double letter = Short vowel!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: What is the difference between 'hopping' and 'hoping'? ('hopping' has double p and short o; 'hoping' has single p and long o)
CCQ 2: Why do we double the 'p' in 'stopped'? (1 syllable + 1 vowel + 1 consonant + vowel suffix -ed)
CCQ 3: Do we double the 't' in 'visiting'? (No, because the stress is on the FIRST syllable VIS-it)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Apply the 1-1-1 doubling rule:
🎯 Item: run + ing = ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: running (doubled n)
🎯 Item: hope + ing = ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: hoping (single p, dropped e)
🎯 Item: visit + ing = ? ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: visiting (unstressed final, no double)
